CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 43 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 1 OF 6




              BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA

         IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                          )
         OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY                            )
         FOR AN ORDER OF THE COMMISSION                               )
         APPROVING ITS NEW EXTRA LARGE LOAD                           )
         TARIFF AND TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF                           )     CASE NO. PUD2026-000046
         SERVICE FOR EXTRA LARGE LOAD                                 )
         CUSTOMERS AND A REGULATORY ASSET TO                          )
         RECOVER COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH                                )
         PORTFOLIO OPTIMIZATION SOFTWARE


         OG&E’S MOTION TO STRIKE PORTIONS OF THE RESPONSIVE TESTIMONY OF
                               ADRIAN J. KIMBROUGH
                 COMES NOW Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E” or “Company”) and

         respectfully moves the Administrative Law Judge to strike portions of the Responsive Testimony

         of Adrian J. Kimbrough filed on behalf of Google LLC, or alternatively rule that such testimony

         shall be disregarded in the determination of legal issues presented in this proceeding. In support

         thereof, OG&E states as follows:

         1.      On September 18, 2026, Google LLC filed the Responsive Testimony of Adrian J.

         Kimbrough. Among other subjects, Mr. Kimbrough advocates for a “Self Supply,” “Bring Your

         Own Generation,” or similar service framework under the proposed Extra Large Power and Light

         Tariff (hereinafter referred to broadly as “Delivery Only Deregulated Generation Election” or

         “DODGE”). See Responsive Testimony of Adrian J. Kimbrough 50:16–58:13.

         2.      Throughout his testimony, Mr. Kimbrough repeatedly acknowledges that he is not an

         attorney. For example, Mr. Kimbrough states: “While I am not an attorney and am not offering a

         legal opinion . . . .” Id. at 5:18–20. He later proceeds to provide legal opinions, stating for instance

         that “self-supply is consistent with Oklahoma law . . . .” Id. at 52:7–9.
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 43 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 6




        3.     Mr. Kimbrough repeatedly provides legal interpretations, legal conclusions, and opinions

        regarding the meaning and effect of Oklahoma statutes, constitutional provisions, judicial

        authority, and Commission precedent on issues to which he testifies.

        4.     For example, Mr. Kimbrough offers testimony regarding:

                   a. Whether proposed self-supply arrangements are consistent with Oklahoma law. Id.

                       at 52:6–10.

                   b. Whether proposed self-supply arrangements violate the Retail Electric Supplier

                       Certified Territory Act. Id. at 52:6–21.

                   c. Whether proposed self-supply arrangements constitute retail choice or retail

                       wheeling. Id. at 53:4–22.

                   d. Whether House Bill 2992 authorizes or permits self-supply frameworks. Id. at 52:9.

                   e. Whether the Commission possesses legal authority to approve such arrangements.

                       Id. at 52:6–53:22.

                   f. Whether prior proceedings before the Commission establish “direct and binding

                       precedent” regarding the legality of self-supply arrangements. Id. at 53:4–10.

                   g. Erroneous claims that the Commission “approved” a joint stipulation that has yet

                       to receive any Final Order. Id. at 53:19–22.

        5.     Particularly concerning are the portions of Mr. Kimbrough’s testimony addressing

        DODGE frameworks in Section M. There, Mr. Kimbrough expressly opines to the Commission

        that self-supply is consistent with Oklahoma law, does not violate the Retail Electric Supplier

        Certified Territory Act, does not constitute retail choice or retail wheeling, and erroneously alleges

        that such arrangements have been determined lawful through “direct and binding administrative




        OG&E’s Motion to Strike                                                                   Page 2 of 6
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 43 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 6




        precedent” that was “approved” in a prior Commission proceeding that is still pending. See

        Kimbrough Responsive Testimony 52:6–53:22.

        6.     These are legal questions.       The interpretation of Oklahoma statutes, constitutional

        provisions, Commission authority, and the legal effect of prior Commission proceedings are

        matters of law, not matters of economic, financial, or tariff-design expertise.

        7.     OG&E does not challenge Mr. Kimbrough’s qualifications to offer testimony concerning

        utility economics, tariff design, cost allocation, or other matters within his professed areas of

        expertise. OG&E challenges only those portions of his testimony that purport to interpret, apply,

        or opine upon Oklahoma law and legal authority despite acknowledging that he lacks legal

        expertise.

        8.     The legal issues Mr. Kimbrough purports to address are presently disputed by the parties.

        As explained in OG&E’s concurrently filed Motion to Amend Procedural Schedule and Establish

        a Briefing Schedule Regarding Proposals for Alternative Service Frameworks, the parties dispute,

        among other matters:

                     a. Whether Oklahoma law authorizes such proposals;

                     b. Whether such proposals are consistent with the Retail Electric Supplier Certified

                        Territory Act;

                     c. Whether such proposals permit or facilitate retail wheeling;

                     d. Whether such proposals are consistent with House Bill 2992; and

                     e. Whether the Commission possesses the jurisdiction and authority to approve such

                        arrangements.




        OG&E’s Motion to Strike                                                              Page 3 of 6
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 43 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/22/2026 - PAGE 4 OF 6




        9.     OG&E has separately requested a focused legal briefing schedule to address these legal

        questions because they involve statutory interpretation, Commission authority, jurisdictional

        considerations, and the interaction of multiple Oklahoma legal frameworks.

        10.    Those questions should be resolved through legal briefing and by the Commission’s

        application of the relevant statutes, constitutional provisions, judicial authorities, Commission

        rules, and Commission orders. They should not be presented through testimony purporting to

        interpret and apply Oklahoma law from witnesses without legal expertise.

        11.    Allowing a non-lawyer expert witness to provide legal interpretations and legal conclusions

        concerning disputed questions of Oklahoma law intrudes upon legal issues better reserved for legal

        advocacy.

        12.    Accordingly, those portions of Mr. Kimbrough’s testimony offering legal interpretations,

        legal conclusions, or legal opinions should be stricken from the record or, alternatively,

        disregarded by the Commission when determining the legal issues presented in this proceeding.

                                             REQUESTED RELIEF

        13.    WHEREFORE, based on the above arguments, OG&E respectfully requests that the

        Administrative Law Judge strike those portions of Kimbrough’s Responsive Testimony at 52:6–

        53:22 that are legal in nature; alternatively rule that those cited questions and answers found at

        pages 52–53 of Mr. Kimbrough’s Responsive Testimony be disregarded and not considered by the

        Commission in determining the legal issues presented in this proceeding; and grant such other and

        further relief as may be just and proper.




        OG&E’s Motion to Strike                                                               Page 4 of 6
